English | [العربية](translations/ar.md) | [Deutsch](translations/de.md) | [Español](translations/es.md) | [Français](translations/fr.md) | [Bahasa Indonesia](translations/id.md) | [日本語](translations/ja.md) | [Português](translations/pt.md) | [Русский](translations/ru.md) | [Türkçe](translations/tr.md) | [Українська](translations/uk.md) | [简体中文](translations/zh-CN.md) | [繁體中文](translations/zh-TW.md) # encrypted-dns-configs Configuration profiles for [DNS over HTTPS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNS_over_HTTPS) and [DNS over TLS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNS_over_TLS). Check out the article for more info: [paulmillr.com/posts/encrypted-dns/](https://paulmillr.com/posts/encrypted-dns/). To add a new provider, or edit an existing one: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Usage Download an HTTPS profile from the table below, then install it. #### iPhone, iPad 1. Open the link in Safari and tap Allow. 2. Within 8 minutes, open Settings > Profile Downloaded (or General > VPN & Device Management) and tap Install. - If installation is refused, Stolen Device Protection may require a familiar location. #### Mac 1. Make sure the file ends in `.mobileconfig`, not `.mobileconfig.txt`, and double-click it. 2. Open System Settings > General > Device Management (macOS 13–14: Privacy & Security > Profiles), double-click the profile and click Install. #### Switching profiles Several profiles can be installed; one is active. Choose it, or "Automatic" for the network's unencrypted DNS: - iPhone, iPad: Settings > General > VPN, DNS & Device Management > DNS - Mac: System Settings > Network > VPN & Filters (macOS 13–14: Filters) - After updating a profile, remove any older copy. #### Checking it works - Open your provider's test page, e.g. [1.1.1.1/help](https://1.1.1.1/help) for Cloudflare. #### Limitations - Prefer HTTPS: DNS over TLS uses port 853, which is easy to block. - These skip encrypted DNS: Firefox in some regions, the App Store, Chrome with "Use secure DNS" on, VPNs, iCloud Private Relay, Little Snitch, LuLu, Personal Hotspot devices, CLI tools like `dig`, and Wi-Fi sign-in pages. - Profiles without `ServerAddresses` look up the resolver's hostname over unencrypted DNS first. ## Providers Tags show what each profile blocks. *mixed content* blocks sites that mix adult and general content; *unspecified* means the provider lists no categories. Filtering changes the `hostname=IP` answer for blocked hosts and can differ by country.
